```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# Theme, palettes and fonts that match the slides
source("R/gph-theme.R")
theme_set(theme_gph())

# Simulated data used by the example figures. Nothing here is real.
set.seed(42)

# A Gaussian process with Matérn correlation, drawn on a grid with random
# Fourier features (smoothness nu = 1.5, scale phi = 0.18)
nu <- 1.5
phi <- 0.18
m <- 2000
omega <- matrix(rnorm(2 * m), ncol = 2) / (phi * sqrt(rchisq(m, df = 2 * nu)))
shift <- runif(m, 0, 2 * pi)
gp_at <- function(xy) {
  sqrt(2 / m) * rowSums(cos(xy %*% t(omega) + rep(shift, each = nrow(xy))))
}

grid <- expand.grid(x = seq(0, 1, length.out = 120), y = seq(0, 1, length.out = 120))
grid$prevalence <- plogis(-1.4 + 0.9 * gp_at(as.matrix(grid)))

n_sites <- 120
sites <- data.frame(x = runif(n_sites), y = runif(n_sites))
sites$tested <- sample(60:180, n_sites, replace = TRUE)
sites$positive <- rbinom(n_sites, sites$tested,
                         plogis(-1.4 + 0.9 * gp_at(as.matrix(sites[, c("x", "y")]))))
sites$observed <- sites$positive / sites$tested

# A stand-in for the predictive standard deviation, growing with the
# distance to the nearest survey, and the probability that prevalence
# exceeds 20%
dist <- sqrt(outer(grid$x, sites$x, "-")^2 + outer(grid$y, sites$y, "-")^2)
grid$sd <- 0.015 + 0.07 * (1 - exp(-apply(dist, 1, min) / 0.08))
grid$exceed <- pnorm((grid$prevalence - 0.2) / grid$sd)

# Monthly proportion of positive collections in three zones
months <- factor(month.abb, levels = month.abb)
seasonal <- function(peak, base, amp) {
  plogis(base + amp * cos(2 * pi * (seq_len(12) - peak) / 12) + rnorm(12, 0, 0.12))
}
zones <- data.frame(
  month = rep(months, 3),
  zone = factor(rep(c("Forest", "Mosaic", "Savanna"), each = 12),
                levels = c("Forest", "Mosaic", "Savanna")),
  positive = c(seasonal(8, -0.4, 0.9), seasonal(9, -1.2, 0.6), seasonal(9, -2.4, 0.5))
)
```

# Writing slides

Text, emphasis, columns and statements

## Lead text and a key message

::: {.lead}
Start a slide with one sentence that says what the audience should take from it.
:::

Body text is set at 28 pixels so that it can be read from the back of a lecture theatre. Use **bold** for key terms, [a gold marker]{.mark} for the one phrase that matters most, and [links](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/) where the audience may want to read more.

::: {.takeaway}
A takeaway block closes the slide with the message to remember.
:::

<!--
Marks are spans: put the words in square brackets and the class in braces.
Add .fragment to any of them and the mark is drawn on the next click while
the words stay in place.
-->

## Ways to mark a word

[A gold marker]{.mark} for the phrase that matters most

[A gold underline]{.underline} for a term you are about to define

A ring around one number, such as [95%]{.circle}

[White on black]{.invert} for a label or a warning

The ~~range~~ scale parameter, for a word you are correcting

*Serif italics* for gentle emphasis

::: {.caption}
Write `[words]{.mark}`, `.underline`, `.circle` or `.invert`, `~~words~~` and `*words*`. Add `.fragment` to draw the mark on the next click, [like this]{.mark .fragment}.
:::

::: {.column width="40%"}

<!-- {.statement} turns the title into a large message in the middle of the slide. -->

## Nearby surveys tell us about places we have not visited {.statement}

Spatial correlation is what lets a geostatistical model borrow strength across locations.

## Key numbers

::: {.stats}
**`r n_sites`** villages surveyed

**`r format(sum(sites$tested), big.mark = ",")`** people tested

**`r scales::percent(mean(sites$observed), accuracy = 1)`** average observed prevalence
:::

Each paragraph inside `.stats` becomes one figure. The first bold text is set large. Use `.stats .large` for a single headline number.

::: {.caption}
Values are computed in R from the simulated data when the slides are rendered.
:::

## A process in steps

::: {.steps}
1. **Explore the data**
   Look at the empirical variogram and the spatial pattern of residuals.
2. **Fit the model**
   Estimate covariate effects and the parameters of the spatial correlation.
3. **Check the predictions**
   Use cross-validation to compare predicted and observed prevalence.
4. **Report with uncertainty**
   Map predictive means alongside exceedance probabilities.
:::

## Three ideas side by side

::: {.cards}
::: {.card .accent}
### Methods

New models for spatial and spatio-temporal health data, with honest uncertainty.
:::

::: {.card}
### Software

Open R packages, such as RiskMap, that make the methods usable by others.
:::

::: {.card}
### Applications

Work with health programmes on decisions about surveillance and control.
:::
:::

Add `.accent` to one card to give it a gold rule.

## The empirical variogram

```{r}
#| label: variogram
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.9
# Simulate an exponential Gaussian process with a nugget at random locations
set.seed(7)
n_vario <- 400
pts <- matrix(runif(2 * n_vario), ncol = 2)
d <- as.matrix(dist(pts))
z <- drop(t(chol(exp(-d / 0.1) + diag(0.1, n_vario))) %*% rnorm(n_vario))

# Binned empirical semivariogram
pairs <- which(upper.tri(d), arr.ind = TRUE)
u <- d[pairs]
g <- 0.5 * (z[pairs[, 1]] - z[pairs[, 2]])^2
bins <- cut(u, breaks = seq(0, 0.6, by = 0.03))
vario <- data.frame(
  u = tapply(u, bins, mean),
  gamma = tapply(g, bins, mean),
  pairs = as.vector(table(bins))
)

# Exponential variogram fitted by weighted least squares (log parameters)
exp_vario <- function(h, tau2, sigma2, phi) tau2 + sigma2 * (1 - exp(-h / phi))
wls <- function(p) {
  sum(vario$pairs * (vario$gamma - exp_vario(vario$u, exp(p[1]), exp(p[2]), exp(p[3])))^2)
}
est <- setNames(exp(optim(log(c(0.1, 1, 0.1)), wls)$par), c("tau2", "sigma2", "phi"))
curve <- data.frame(u = seq(0, 0.6, length.out = 200))
curve$gamma <- exp_vario(curve$u, est[["tau2"]], est[["sigma2"]], est[["phi"]])
practical_range <- log(20) * est[["phi"]]

ggplot(vario, aes(u, gamma)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = practical_range, colour = gph_grey,
             linewidth = 0.5, linetype = "22") +
  geom_line(data = curve, colour = gph_colours[["blue"]], linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(colour = gph_ink, size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = practical_range + 0.01, y = 0.15, hjust = 0,
           label = "Practical range", family = gph_font,
           colour = gph_grey, size = 5.6) +
  scale_x_continuous("Distance between locations", limits = c(0, 0.6),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  scale_y_continuous("Semivariance", limits = c(0, NA),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05)))
```

::: {.caption}
Simulated data at `r n_vario` locations. Points are binned empirical semivariances. The line is an exponential variogram fitted by weighted least squares, with estimated scale parameter `r round(est[["phi"]], 3)` and practical range `r round(practical_range, 2)`.
:::

## Colour keys in the text

```{r}
#| label: zones
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4
# Direct labels at the end of each line, pushed apart when they are close
last <- zones[zones$month == "Dec", ]
last <- last[order(last$positive), ]
last$label_y <- last$positive
for (i in 2:nrow(last)) {
  last$label_y[i] <- max(last$label_y[i], last$label_y[i - 1] + 0.06)
}

ggplot(zones, aes(month, positive, colour = zone, group = zone)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(data = last, aes(y = label_y, label = zone), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.25,
            family = gph_font, size = 6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_gph(guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 1.6))) +
  scale_y_continuous("Positive collections", labels = scales::label_percent(),
                     limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = NULL)
```

Write [Forest]{.key .turquoise}, [Mosaic]{.key .orange} and [Savanna]{.key .purple} to link the text to the figure without coloured text, or tint a marker as in [Forest]{.mark .turquoise}. Add `.line` or `.dot` to change the key's shape.

<!--
scale_colour_gph_highlight("Forest") draws the named groups in the

## One group in colour

```{r}
#| label: zones-highlight
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4
# Forest last, so that it is drawn on top of the grey lines
zones_front <- transform(zones, zone = factor(zone, levels = c("Mosaic", "Savanna", "Forest")))

ggplot(zones_front, aes(month, positive, colour = zone, group = zone)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.1) +
  geom_point(size = 2.6) +
  geom_text(data = last, aes(y = label_y, label = zone), hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.25,
            family = gph_font, size = 6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_gph_highlight("Forest", guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = expansion(add = c(0.4, 1.6))) +
  scale_y_continuous("Positive collections", labels = scales::label_percent(),
                     limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = NULL)
```

Only in [Forest]{.key .turquoise} does positivity pass 40%. The other zones stay on the plot in grey, for context.

## Tables

| Question | Model output | Shown as |
|:---------|:-------------|:---------|
| Where is prevalence highest? | Predictive mean of prevalence | A map |
| How sure are we? | Predictive standard deviation | A second map with its own scale |
| Has a threshold been crossed? | Exceedance probability $P\{p(x) > c \mid y\}$ | A map on a fixed 0 to 1 scale |
| What is happening across a district? | Areal average with a predictive interval | A number with its interval |

Tables have clean rules and no shading. Keep them short and round the numbers.

# Models and code {.dark}

Equations, R code, callouts and references

## A model and what each term means

::: {.equation}
$$
\log\left\{\frac{p(x_i)}{1 - p(x_i)}\right\} = d(x_i)^\top \beta + S(x_i) + Z_i
$$
:::

::: {.terms}
$Y_i \sim \text{Bin}\{n_i, p(x_i)\}$

Number of positive tests among $n_i$ people sampled at location $x_i$

$d(x_i)^\top \beta$

Effects of covariates such as elevation or rainfall

$S(x)$

Zero-mean Gaussian process with variance $\sigma^2$ and correlation $\rho(u) = \exp(-u / \phi)$

$\phi$

Scale parameter of the spatial correlation. The practical range is $\log(20)\,\phi \approx 3\phi$

$Z_i$

Unstructured variation, independent $\text{N}(0, \tau^2)$
:::

## Code

```{r}
#| label: code-example
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
#| code-line-numbers: "|1-3|5-11|13"
library(RiskMap)

data(loaloa)

fit <- glgpm(
  NO_INF ~ log(ELEVATION) + gp(),
  data = loaloa,
  family = "binomial",
  denominator = NO_EXAM,
  distance_units = "km"
)

summary(fit)
```

Set `echo: true` on a chunk to show its code. Add `code-line-numbers: "|1-3|5-11"` to step through the lines on each click.

Model-based geostatistics was introduced by @diggle1998. Book-length treatments are @diggle2007 and @diggle2019, and @giorgi2026 covers the methods in R.

## A prevalence map without its uncertainty is only half an answer {.statement .dark}

Show predictive standard deviations or exceedance probabilities beside every map of predicted prevalence.

## Conclusions

- **Spatial models** borrow strength from nearby surveys
- **Uncertainty** belongs on the map, not in a footnote
- **Open software** lets programmes use the methods

## Slide classes

| Class | Use it on | Effect |
|:--------|:---------------|:-------------------|
| `.statement` | slide heading | One large message |
| `.closing` | slide heading | Closing slide with the motif |
| `.dark` | section, statement or closing slide | White on the brand black |
| `.photo` | slide heading | Background image fills the slide |
| `.outline` | slide heading | List of sections, filled in for you |
| `.no-title` | slide heading | Hides the title bar |
| `.unnumbered` | section heading | Section slide without a number |
| `.backup` | section heading | Starts the uncounted backup slides |

## Layout classes

| Class | Use it on | Effect |
|:--------|:---------------|:-------------------|
| `.fill` | div around one image | Image fills the space below the title |
| `.framed` | image | Thin border, for screenshots |
| `.logo-row` | div of images | Lines up partner or funder logos |
| `.caption`, `.small` | div or span | Grey metadata text |
| `.source` | div | Source line pinned to the bottom |
| `.papers` | div of images or PDFs | Tops of first pages, or `.full` pages |
| `.people` | div around a list | Grid of people with photos or initials |
